question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate that can inspect assistant text and hold risky tool calls before execution, or keep confirmation limited to existing exec/plugin approval primitives?
rationale: The request adds a public config surface and changes the core tool execution authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the risk classifier, timeout, channel routing, transcript, and compatibility semantics unilaterally.

options.title: Design a core confirmation gate
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default, schema-backed confirmation policy that runs before side-effecting tool execution and composes with existing approval hooks.

options.title: Keep existing approval primitives only
options.body: Close this as out of scope and direct users to exec approvals, plugin before_tool_call.requireApproval, and custom trusted tool policies.

options.title: Fold into broader HITL interrupt design
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer it to a unified response-gate or generic interrupt primitive that also covers related HITL workflows.

recommendation.title: Design a core confirmation gate
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default, schema-backed confirmation policy that runs before side-effecting tool execution and composes with existing approval hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hook/config/runtime ownership signals make this the best available maintainer-routing owner for the core boundary decision.
